title: Firehall Burnt Ends Platter
seoTitle: Firehall Burnt Ends Platter | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Kansas City-style burnt ends without waiting on a full packer cook
subtitle: Caramelized brisket point cubes, sticky glaze, and pickles for ten
description: Adapted from classic Kansas City burnt-end tradition (Amazing Ribs, BBQ Pit Boys): brisket point smokes until tender, gets cubed, glazed, and finished until the edges turn sticky and charred.

ingredients.name: brisket point
ingredients.notes: or untrimmed point from a packer

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Firehall Burnt Ends Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the point
steps.instruction: Pat point dry. Mix salt, pepper, brown sugar, paprika, and garlic powder; rub all sides. Rest 15 minutes while smoker heats to 275°F.

steps.title: Smoke until tender
steps.instruction: Smoke point fat-side up at 275°F until bark is set and internal temp reaches 165°F, about 4 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap in foil with a splash of apple cider vinegar. Continue at 275°F until probe-tender and 203°F internal, about 2–3 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and cube
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 30 minutes. Cube point into 1-inch bites, discarding excess hard fat and gristle. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer BBQ sauce, honey, vinegar, and butter until glossy. Toss cubed burnt ends to coat evenly. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Caramelize the edges
steps.instruction: Spread glazed cubes on sheet pans. Return to smoker or 375°F oven 15–20 minutes, stirring once, until edges char and glaze sets sticky.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: Hold covered at 170°F with foil vented slightly. Serve on a platter with pickles and white bread for burnt-end sandwiches. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered at 325°F with extra sauce. Chop into mac and cheese or loaded fries. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Point needs 203°F—lean on probe tenderness, not the clock.
Stir once during the glaze bake so edges caramelize evenly.
If you only have a flat, save it for sliced service; burnt ends want point fat.
tonightSpread: Burnt ends in a hotel pan with extra glaze on the side.
Pickles and white bread for quick sandwiches.
leftovers: Burnt-end grilled cheese with extra pickles.
Fold into baked beans for a smoky second-day pot.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Burnt ends are the reward cut—loud, sweet, and smoky. They hold warm in a covered pan and disappear fast at the line.
mealPrepNotes: Smoke point early. Cube and glaze right before service or hold glazed cubes covered at 170°F up to 45 minutes. Re-crisp under broiler 2 minutes if they soften.
